![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194111/assets/bdf61d89183886da1f519bad64221e7fdafd16a9ae5eb2c588728398f10477b5.png)

What are the equations of the horizontal asymptotes of $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?
question.worked_solution:
- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ becomes larger and larger without bound. We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to \infty \,\text{as}\,x\to \infty 
$$

This does not give us a horizontal asymptote.

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ gets more and more negative without bound. We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to -\infty \,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty 
$$

This does not give us a horizontal asymptote.

choices.value: The function has no horizontal asymptotes

responses.value: The function has no horizontal asymptotes
